proposals.before: Under the Taizong he was styled the "Fourth Beile"; because Qi Chongge was well versed in letters and history, he was put in charge of secretarial work.
proposals.after: When the Taizong was [still] styled the "Fourth Beile," because Qi Chongge was well versed in letters and history, he was put in charge of secretarial work.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太宗時號「四貝勒」attributes the Fourth Beile style to Taizong (Hong Taiji), not to Qi Chongge; the English wrongly makes Qi Chongge the Fourth Beile.

proposals.before: In the Taizong's time he was styled the "Fourth Beile"; because Qi Chongge was skilled in letters and history, he was ordered to manage secretarial work.
proposals.after: In the time when the Taizong was styled the "Fourth Beile," because Qi Chongge was skilled in letters and history, he was ordered to manage secretarial work.
proposals.reason: Same referent error as the idiomatic field: 四貝勒 names Taizong, not Qi Chongge.

proposals.before: Qi Chongge, for failing to advise Prince Hooge to join the emperor in escorting the army and for privately visiting his estate that same day, was liable to death; the sentence was commuted—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was flogged, and was placed under the Prince Regent.
proposals.after: Qi Chongge, for failing to advise Prince Yu Dodo to join the emperor in escorting the army and for privately visiting his estate that same day, was liable to death; the sentence was commuted—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was flogged, and was placed under the Prince Regent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 豫親王多鐸 is Prince Yu Dodo, not Prince Hooge (豪格).

proposals.before: Qi Chongge, for not advising Prince Hooge Dotuo to accompany the emperor in escorting him and on that same day privately going to his estate, was liable to death; the order was to show leniency—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was whipped, and was placed under the Prince Regent.
proposals.after: Qi Chongge, for not advising Prince Yu Dodo to accompany the emperor in escorting him and on that same day privately going to his estate, was liable to death; the order was to show leniency—he was stripped of office, had his ears pierced and was whipped, and was placed under the Prince Regent.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise mistranslates 豫親王多鐸 as Prince Hooge Dotuo; the person is Dodo.

proposals.before: In the sixth year he was given the added titles of Junior Tutor and Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: In the sixth year he was given the added titles of Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太子太傅 is Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; the idiomatic English wrongly renders 太傅 as Junior Preceptor.

proposals.before: Soon he was given the added titles of Junior Preceptor and Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: Soon he was given the added titles of Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太子太師 is Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Junior Tutor understates 太師.

proposals.before: In Shunzhi 1 he was restored to his former office and rose in succession to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
proposals.after: In Shunzhi 1 he was restored to his former office and rose in succession to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
proposals.reason: 少詹事 is an office in the Household of the Heir Apparent (詹事府), not 太子太保/Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; the English conflates distinct titles.

proposals.before: In the first year of Shunzhi he was restored to his former office and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
proposals.after: In the first year of Shunzhi he was restored to his former office and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 少詹事 as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; retain the Household office sense.

proposals.before: If Mingxia were again condemned, that would be untrustworthy."
proposals.after: If Mingxia were condemned again, that would make me untrustworthy."
proposals.reason: Chinese 是為不信 means the emperor would thereby become untrustworthy; the literal omits the first-person consequence present in the idiomatic and the Chinese.

proposals.before: He once told me: "If hair is kept and Han dress restored, the realm will at once be at peace."
proposals.after: He once told me: 'If hair is kept and Han dress restored, the realm will at once be at peace.'
proposals.reason: The embedded quotation is nested inside Ning Wanwo's memorial quotation; matching the literal's single quotes avoids corrupted nested double-quote boundaries.

proposals.before: Censor Yang Yi discussed ministry recommendations that skipped proper order; Zhengzong argued with him and the two clung to each other in mutual abuse.
proposals.after: Censor Yang Yi discussed ministry recommendations that skipped proper order; Zhengzong argued with him and they stubbornly exchanged mutual abuse.
proposals.reason: 執相詬詈 means holding fast while exchanging abuse, not physically clinging together.

proposals.before: he also stated that Zhilin had prompted Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an to recommend Prefect Shen Lingshi, who was soon memorialized against by Governor Li Huizu—this was evidence of faction forming.
proposals.after: he also stated that Zhilin had prompted Minister of Rites Hu Shi'an to recommend Prefect Shen Lingshi, who was soon memorialized against by Governor-General Li Huizu—this was evidence of faction forming.
proposals.reason: 總督 denotes Governor-General, not the lower office 巡撫 usually rendered Governor.

decisions.after: When the Taizong was still styled the "Fourth Beile," because Qi Chongge was well versed in letters and history, he was put in charge of secretarial work.
decisions.reason: 太宗時號「四貝勒」attributes 四貝勒 to Taizong, not Qi Chongge; the original wrongly styles Qi Chongge the Fourth Beile. The proposed fix is right in referent but the bracketed [still] is not natural English.
Same referent error in the literal: 四貝勒 names Taizong; the proposed temporal clause correctly attaches the style to him, not to Qi Chongge.
不啟豫親王多鐸 names Prince Yu Dodo; rendering him as Prince Hooge is a clear misidentification.
Literal likewise misreads 豫親王多鐸 as Prince Hooge Dotuo; Prince Yu Dodo is the correct person.
太子太傅 is Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; Junior Preceptor would be 少師, so the original under-ranks 太傅.
太子太師 is Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; Junior Tutor understates 太師.
少詹事 is Junior Supervisor in the Household of the Heir Apparent (詹事府), confirmed by the next unit's 詹事府裁; it is not 太子太保/Junior Guardian.
Same 少詹事 mistranslation in the literal; the Household office sense is required.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 累遷少詹事，兼國子監祭酒

decisions.reason: 是為不信 in the emperor's speech means condemning Mingxia again would make the speaker himself untrustworthy; the original literal drops that first-person consequence.
The wording already matches 嘗謂臣曰…留發复衣冠，天下即太平; switching nested double quotes to single quotes is punctuation style only, not a semantic repair.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 嘗謂臣曰：'留發复衣冠，天下即太平。

decisions.reason: 執相詬詈 means they persisted in mutual abuse, not that they physically clung together; the proposed wording restores that sense.
總督 is Governor-General, distinct from 巡撫 usually rendered Governor; the replacement corrects the office rank.
